tree: Clear reasons for every routing decision.
Each order shows why it went where it did, and you can change the weighting or send any order somewhere else by hand.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 14px; padding: 20px;

tree: How does it pick the location for an order?
By who has all the items in stock, who is closest to the customer and what it costs to ship, weighted the way you choose.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Can I override where an order ships from?
Yes. Any order can be moved to another location by hand, and the reason is kept.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Orders going out from the same place are grouped into one pick list sorted by shelf, so staff collect everything in one pass.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Will it split an order across locations?
Only if you allow it. By default it prefers one location that can fill the whole order.

tree.style: background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.08); border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px;

tree: Does it work with my own delivery riders?
Yes. Orders routed to a location can go to your riders or to a shipping carrier.
